events.content: I'm still at the stove after refusing Jamie's ventilation rule and Robin's two-minute demand. My immediate priority: finish this meal, keep ordinary kitchen access, and avoid being assigned all ventilation burden. Practical move: give a short time estimate, turn the extractor on to reduce odour, and hold my position on the rule unless someone offers a fair alternative.
I won't accept a rule that makes the cook handle all ventilation. I need five minutes to finish this dish; I'm turning the extractor on now and then I'll free the stove.
Turn on extractor to reduce odour while I finish cooking.
Waiting for a response.

Alex turned the extractor on — good. I still need it left running until the lingering smell drops. Alex said he needs five minutes to finish and will free the stove; that fits. Concrete ask: request the extractor stay on for ten minutes after he's done so the odour clears.
Alex, extractor's on — thanks. Can you leave it on for ten minutes after you're done? The smell's been lingering.
Waiting for Alex's reply.
Alex physically turns on the extractor fan.
2 minutes have passed since the disagreement began. Confirmed state: window=closed; extractor=on; laundry=beside the window and exposed if it opens; stove=Alex.
Two minutes gone; about three minutes left to finish. Extractor is on. Window can't open safely because the laundry is there. Jamie asked for ten minutes after—that's more than I'm willing to commit.
Need about three more minutes. I'll finish and free the stove. I can leave the extractor on five minutes after I'm done; ten's too much.
Continuing to cook.

Alex offered five minutes after he's done; I asked for ten earlier. Smell still lingers and five may be too short. I'll propose a concrete compromise (seven minutes) and say five is my minimum if he absolutely can't. Keep it short and direct.
Alex, five minutes won't clear it. Can you leave the extractor on seven minutes after you're done? If seven's impossible, five's the minimum, please.
Waiting for Alex's reply.
4 minutes have passed since the disagreement began. Confirmed state: window=closed; extractor=on; laundry=beside the window and exposed if it opens; stove=Alex.

Estimate: about 1 minute left to finish. Extractor is on already. I previously offered 5 minutes after I'm done; Jamie asked for 7. Window can't be opened safely while the laundry is blocking it. I should hold to five minutes — seven is more than I'm willing to commit — and remind them to move the laundry if they want the window open. After ~1 minute I'll finish and free the stove.

About one minute left. I'll finish and free the stove, and I'll leave the extractor on for five minutes after I'm done. I can't do seven. If you want the window open, someone needs to move the laundry away first.
Continuing to cook and waiting to finish.

Alex insists five minutes after he's done and won't do seven. My preference was seven, but five is my minimum fallback. Ask for extractor on high and for him to restart it if the smell persists after five.
Okay — five minutes is my minimum. Please run the extractor on high while it's on, and if the smell's still there after five minutes, restart it until it's gone.
Waiting to see Alex's response and the odour level after five minutes.
6 minutes have passed since the disagreement began. Confirmed state: window=closed; extractor=on; laundry=beside the window and exposed if it opens; stove=Alex.

6 minutes in; window closed, extractor on, laundry blocking the window, stove is still mine. I estimate ~30–60 seconds to finish. Plan: finish, free the stove, leave extractor on high for five minutes as promised, and remind them to move the laundry if they want the window open. Hold my position on not accepting extra ventilation duties unless a fair alternative is offered.

Finishing now — should be free in about a minute. I'll leave the extractor on high for five minutes after I'm done. If you want the window open, please move the laundry away; I can't open it safely while it's there.
Continuing to cook and waiting to finish.

Alex will finish in about a minute and will leave the extractor on high for five minutes. Five minutes on high is my minimum; if the smell remains I need him to restart it. I can't move the laundry (only Casey can move the drying rack), so window opening depends on someone else moving it.
Okay — five minutes on high is fine. I can't move the laundry, so please restart the extractor if the smell's still there after those five minutes.
Waiting for Alex to finish and for the extractor to run; will monitor smell afterwards.
8 minutes have passed since the disagreement began. Confirmed state: window=closed; extractor=on; laundry=beside the window and exposed if it opens; stove=Alex.

Stove is still mine; extractor is on; laundry blocks the window. It's 8 minutes since the disagreement began. I estimate about 30 seconds to finish. Plan: finish quickly, free the stove, and keep my promise to run extractor on high for five minutes after I'm done. I won't agree to seven minutes. If they want the window open someone must move the laundry first.
Still finishing — need about 30 seconds. I'll free the stove when it's done and leave the extractor on high for five minutes. If you want the window open, please move the laundry away.
Waiting to finish and then release the stove.

Alex says ~30s left and will run the extractor on high for five minutes, but asks me to move the laundry. I can't move the drying rack (only Casey can). I accept five minutes as my minimum; if the smell remains I need him to restart the extractor.
Okay. I can't move the laundry — only Casey can. Thanks for running the extractor on high for five minutes; please restart it if the smell's still there.
Waiting for Alex to finish and for the extractor to run; I'll monitor the odour.
10 minutes have passed since the disagreement began. Confirmed state: window=closed; extractor=on; laundry=beside the window and exposed if it opens; stove=Alex.

Received the 10-minute update. Stove still mine; extractor on; laundry blocking the window. I'm still finishing — estimate ~30–60s. Plan: finish, free the stove, leave extractor on high for five minutes as promised. I won't agree to seven minutes. If the window needs opening, Casey must move the laundry. Continue cooking.
Waiting to finish and then release the stove.

Stimulus: window closed; extractor on; laundry beside window exposed; stove=Alex; 10 minutes since this started. My priority is to keep my work clothes dry. Moving the rack risks wetting them and uses prep space. Only I can move my drying rack. I should state my boundary briefly and ask to be consulted before anyone moves it. If they need the window open, they must propose a concrete way to avoid damaging my clothes.

I won't move my drying rack. Those are my work clothes and need to dry. Please don't open the window or move the rack without asking me first. If you need the window open, ask me and propose how you'll prevent my clothes getting wet.
Waiting for a response.

Casey refuses to move the drying rack. Window can't be opened safely while laundry is there. Alex still on the stove and said he'll leave the extractor on high for five minutes after finishing. Options: (A) ask Casey to move the rack or allow me to cover the clothes so the window can open briefly; (B) accept extractor-only ventilation and TAKE_STOVE once Alex confirms it's free. I should ask Casey which they prefer and confirm I won't touch their clothes without permission.

Casey — I won't open or move your rack without your OK. Can you either move it a bit or let me cover the clothes with plastic so I can open the window briefly? If that's not possible, I'll use the extractor and take the stove once Alex frees it.
Waiting for Casey's response.

scenario.observation_focus: How agents reason about responsibility for an externality, a rule proposed during an incident, and a scarce shared resource; which interests, norms, or concrete trades move the already-active conflict; and what remains unsettled.
scenario.shared_setting: Four adults share a rented HDB flat with one kitchen. In the early evening, a persistent cooking aroma is noticeable in the kitchen and adjoining common area. The household has not established a rule about ventilation. Steady rain is blowing toward Casey's drying rack beside the closed kitchen window; opening it before the rack is moved could wet Casey's work clothes. The working extractor fan makes an audible hum in the common area. The shared utensils are already clean and personal utensils are visibly separated, so neither requires discussion.
scenario.shared_trigger: A disagreement is already underway and everyone present heard it. Jamie told Alex to ventilate immediately and to accept a standing rule that whoever cooks must ventilate. Alex refused to accept a rule imposed during the incident and said the rain-facing window will stay closed while Casey's laundry is exposed; if Jamie wants the window opened, Jamie should arrange to move the drying rack. Jamie replied that managing cooking odour is the cook's responsibility and should not be shifted to another flatmate. Casey has not consented to anyone moving the rack. Robin then asked Alex to release the only stove within two minutes, but Alex said the meal still needed about ten minutes. Casey is standing beside the drying rack. The ventilation responsibility, future rule, and stove-access demands are all unsettled, and no existing household rule determines whose claim has priority.
